items_full.label: C031 · Australia · 1943 · Threepence (3d) · AUD

payload.story: A 1943 Australian threepence, struck in the middle of World War II. King George VI is on the front, and the back shows three stalks of wheat by George Kruger Gray, a design used since 1938 — before the war began. It's made of real silver, which is why it feels different from today's coins in your hand.

record.metal: .925 sterling silver · 1.41 g · 16 mm · plain · circulated / toned · white 2×2 staple flip
record.design: obverse George VI · IND:IMP still in legend · reverse three wheat stalks · AUSTRALIA · THREE PENCE · 1943 · S

items_full.label: C033 · France · 1969 · 1/2 franc · FRF

payload.story: A 1969 French half franc. The front shows the Sower — a woman scattering seeds at sunrise, one of France's most loved coin designs, first drawn by Oscar Roty around 1887. The back carries France's motto: liberty, equality, brotherhood.

record.metal: nickel · 4.50 g · 19.5 mm · reeded · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip
record.specs: thickness ~1.8 mm · coin alignment · type specs shared with nickel Semeuse ½ Fr 1965–2001 (KM#931.1) · magnetic Ni (not Ag)
record.design: obverse La Semeuse left (Oscar Roty) · reverse 1/2 FRANC · olive sprig · LIBERTE · EGALITE · FRATERNITE · date

items_full.label: C048 · Germany · 1993 · 1 Deutsche Mark · DEM

payload.story: A 1993 German 1 Deutsche Mark. The eagle with outstretched wings is Germany's federal eagle, a symbol of strength; the oak sprigs are on the other side, framing the value. The Deutsche Mark was one of the world's most trusted currencies until the euro replaced it in 2002.

record.metal: CuNi · 5.50 g · 23.5 mm · ornamented (arabesque) · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip
record.design: Bundesadler · value 1 between oak sprigs / DEUTSCHE MARK (Josef Bernhart)

items_full.label: C049 · France · 1989 · 10 francs · FRF

payload.story: A 1989 French 10 franc piece. The front shows the Spirit of Liberty, taken from the gilded statue on top of the July Column at the Place de la Bastille in Paris. The back has the value 10F with liberty, equality, fraternity. It was one of France's first two-metal coins — a silvery center set in a golden ring.

record.metal: bimetallic (Ni center / Al-bronze ring) · 6.50 g · 23 mm · reeded · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip
record.specs: thickness 2.1 mm · coin alignment · type specs shared with Génie 10 F 1988–2000 (KM#964.1)
record.design: obverse Génie de la Liberté (after François Rude · Bastille column) · reverse 10 F · LIBERTE · EGALITE · FRATERNITE · date · RF

items_full.label: C050 · Germany · 1982 · 1 Deutsche Mark · DEM

payload.story: A 1982 German 1 Deutsche Mark. The federal eagle spreads its wings on one side; two oak sprigs frame the value on the other. This was everyday pocket money in West Germany for decades — the kind of coin your change came in at the bakery.

record.mint: unknown (letter under date unclear (soft D/G candidate))
record.metal: CuNi · 5.50 g · 23.5 mm · ornamented (arabesque) · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip
record.design: Bundesadler · value 1 between oak sprigs / DEUTSCHE MARK (Josef Bernhart)

items_full.label: C057 · Germany · 1982 · 50 Pfennig · DEM

payload.story: A 1982 German 50 pfennig. A woman kneels to plant a young oak on the front, honoring the 'rubble women' who rebuilt Germany's ruined cities after World War II. The other side carries the value, 50 PFENNIG, with BUNDESREPUBLIK DEUTSCHLAND.

record.mint: No mint mark on this side — German 50 pfennig carries the mint letter on the value side; this photo shows the oak-planter (Baumpflanzerin) side, flip needed to read the letter

record.design: Trümmerfrau planting oak sapling (Richard M. Werner / Gerda Werner) · Bundesadler value side

items_full.label: C068 · Switzerland · 1963 · 20 rappen · CHF

payload.story: A 1963 Swiss 20 rappen. The front shows Libertas, the Roman goddess of liberty, with braided hair and a tiara. The Swiss have used this same proud design since the 1800s — if it works, don't fix it.

record.metal: CuNi 75/25 · 4.00 g · 21.05 mm · plain · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip

items_full.label: C069 · Jamaica · 1975 · 50 cents · JMD

payload.story: A 1975 Jamaican 50 cent piece. The coat of arms shows a crocodile on a log on top, held up by a man and woman of the Taino people who lived on the island first. The motto reads 'Out of Many, One People.'

record.metal: cupronickel · 12.43 g · 31.37 mm · reeded · circulated · white 2×2 staple flip · decagonal (10-sided)

payload.story: A 1954 five-centavo coin from Argentina, from Juan Perón's second presidency. The side shown has a large 5 with CENTAVOS and the date, and REPUBLICA ARGENTINA around the rim; the other side of this series carries a portrait of José de San Martín, the general who led Argentina to independence.
